LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND SPEAKING: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency, part of Strand 9 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: which have the sounds /eə/ /aʊ/ and /h/, • speak at the right speed, 1. Why should you speak accurately and without hesitations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say words and phrases with the sounds /eə/, /aʊ/ and /h / correctly,

2. practise saying tongue twisters with the selected sounds,

3. recite poems on lifestyle diseases with words

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say words and phrases with the sounds /eə/, /aʊ/ and /h / correctly,
2. practise saying tongue twisters with the selected sounds,
3. recite poems on lifestyle diseases with words

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they make short

videos of the poetry recitation or narration and share them with friends or peers.

• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to speak more fluently and with confidence is developed as they make short

speeches expressively, accurately and without hesitations.

Values:
Responsibility: This is cultivated in the learner as they undertake assigned roles while delivering speeches on

lifestyle diseases.

Peace is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance while reciting choral verses with peers

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle diseases: The learner’s grasp of health issues is enhanced as they make short speeches on lifestyle diseases

expressively, accurately and without hesitations.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Effective use of fixed expressions, proverbs and similes is related to use of these expressions in public speaking in

Kiswahili.
